items.title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Co-Chairs 23rd Session of India–Italy Joint Commission for Economic Cooperation in Rome
items.summary: Mr. Antonio Tajani, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Italy, in Rome on 18 November 2026. The Ministers reviewed the progress of bilateral economic and commercial cooperation and discussed measures to expand trade, investment and industrial partnerships.

facts.text: The Ministers also welcomed the successful conclusion of negotiations on the India–EU Free Trade Agreement and discussed its potential to expand market access, increase trade and investment flows and strengthen supply chains.
In this context, they reaffirmed the shared target of achieving €20 billion in bilateral trade by 2029 and emphasised the need to diversify trade and scale up investments.

The Minister also addressed the India–Italy Business and Innovation Forum in Rome, which brought together senior government leaders, industry associations and Italian companies, along with around 80 Indian business delegates, including 12 startups.

Ahead of the Forum, Shri Goyal interacted with the Indian business delegation on opportunities for Indian businesses in Italy and the wider European market, including those arising from the India–EU Free Trade Agreement.

items.title: Union Ministry of Health Proposes Incorporation of Good Storage and Distribution Practices into Drugs Rules, 1945
items.summary: The proposal aims to ensure that the quality, safety, efficacy and integrity of pharmaceutical products are maintained throughout the distribution chain, from the manufacturer or importer to the point of supply to the patient. The proposed framework builds upon the GSDP guidance developed by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

facts.text: The guidelines seek to ensure the quality and identity of pharmaceutical products at every stage of the distribution process, including procurement, purchasing, storage, distribution, transportation, documentation and record-keeping.

It will also promote robust documentation, record-keeping and traceability, while enhancing accountability among manufacturers, importers, wholesalers, distributors, stockists and other entities involved in the distribution process.
This will support the availability of pharmaceutical products of assured quality to patients and healthcare providers.

Stakeholders and members of the public are invited to submit their objections and suggestions, if any, to the Under Secretary (Drugs Regulation), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, U-6, Work Hall, C Wing, First Floor, Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi - 110001, or via email at…
